title: Coding Set 08: Frequency Sorting & Run-Length Compression
description: Reported string processing problems: sorting characters by descending frequency with ASCII tie-breaking and RLE compression.

problems.title: Sort Characters by Frequency
problems.statement: Given a string S, rearrange its characters in descending order of their frequency in S. If two characters have the same frequency, the character with the smaller ASCII value must come first.
problems.inputFormat: A single line containing non-empty string S.

starterCode.python:
import sys

s = sys.stdin.readline().strip()
# Write your solution here

solutions.python:
import sys
from collections import Counter

s = sys.stdin.readline().strip()
cnt = Counter(s)
ordered = sorted(cnt.items(), key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))
print(''.join(ch * f for ch, f in ordered))

problems.timeComplexity: O(N + K log K) where K <= 256 (effectively O(N)).
edgeCases: All characters unique -> sorted purely by ASCII

problems.title: String Compression (Run-Length Encoding)
problems.statement: Compress a string S by replacing consecutive repeated runs of a character with `<char><count>`. Note: unlike some variants, ALWAYS include the count (even if 1), UNLESS the compressed string is NOT strictly shorter than S—in that case, print the original string S unchanged.
problems.inputFormat: A single line containing string S.
problems.outputFormat: Compressed string if strictly shorter than S, otherwise original S.

starterCode.python:
import sys

s = sys.stdin.readline().strip()
# Write your solution here

solutions.python:
import sys

s = sys.stdin.readline().strip()
out = []
i = 0
n = len(s)
while i < n:
    j = i
    while j < n and s[j] == s[i]:
        j += 1
    out.append(f'{s[i]}{j - i}')
    i = j
comp = ''.join(out)
print(comp if len(comp) < n else s)

edgeCases: Equal compressed length (`aabbcc` -> len 6 == 6) must keep original
